inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted share count of 647m from the H1 FY2026 results memo table (30 June 2026). Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows and there are no buybacks.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, share-based payments line in the underlying EBITDA reconciliation (GBP 12.1m, group incl. CEE). No separate equity-award withholding-tax line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0). H1 FY2026 continuing charge was GBP 11m, so the forward path is anchored at ~0.45% of revenue, not the FY2025 0.23%.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp). Model-to-quote factor is exactly 100 (unit conversion, not a market rate). Magnitude check: weighted IV in pence is the same order as the pence quote. Bridge items converted at Yahoo spot on 2026-11-18: GBPUSD 1.3134 (BetMGM), EURGBP 0.8348 (CEE).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T17:09:32Z (LSE regular session close; not an after-hours print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP build: 10-year gilt ~4.5% risk-free, ~5% ERP, equity beta ~1.2 gives cost of equity ~10.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~6.5% (term loans and high-yield bonds), ~4.9% after tax; target debt weight ~40-45% gives ~8.0%, rounded up to 8.5% for sub-investment-grade leverage of 3.1x. The same 8.5% is used in all three scenarios: regulatory, tax and litigation risk is charged in the flows and the scenario weights, not again in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. lease_cost_pct_path carries three fixed cash charges that sit outside underlying EBITDA: IFRS 16 lease payments, principal plus interest (GBP 33m in H1 FY2026 continuing, ~GBP 68m a year); the TAB NZ revenue-share payment (GBP 35m in H1, guided c.GBP 70m for FY2026), which the company deducts below EBITDA in its own adjusted cash flow; and an allowance of ~0.5% of revenue for recurring restructuring and legal costs the company reports as separately disclosed items. Lease liabilities of GBP 335m are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt (adjusted net debt 3,599 less 335 = 3,264), and da_pct_path is underlying D&A excluding right-of-use depreciation.
inputs.nci_treatment: The only material non-controlling interest is the 32.5% of Entain CEE held by EMMA Capital. CEE is excluded from the flows entirely (reported as discontinued) and only Entain's own 67.5% stake is added in the equity bridge, so NCI is charged once. The GBP 587m put liability over the minority (FY2025) is an obligation to buy that stake at fair value and is value-neutral on this basis; it is not deducted.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF on CONTINUING operations (UK&I, International incl. Australia/NZ, Brazil, Italy; Corporate), with two sum-of-parts additions in the equity bridge. Reason: Entain is an operating company whose value is a cash-flow stream, so the owner-FCF route applies; but two pieces are outside consolidated underlying EBITDA and would otherwise be lost. (1) BetMGM, the 50% US joint venture, is equity-accounted: its JV income is not in underlying EBITDA, so its value is added in the bridge (matching-asset rule). BetMGM parent fees paid to Entain (GBP 7m in H1 FY2026) ARE in revenue and EBITDA, so BetMGM is valued on EBITDA after parent fees to avoid counting them twice. (2) Entain CEE (Croatia, Poland) has been reported as discontinued since the 25 June 2026 agreement to sell a 20% interest as the first step of a phased exit; it is excluded from base revenue and all driver paths and valued in the bridge at the transaction price. Base revenue is FY2025 group revenue 5,259.4 less the CEE segment 521.7 (FY2025 annual report segment note); FY2025 continuing underlying EBITDA on the same basis is 976.4 (20.6%). Statutory net income is negative in FY2023-FY2025 because of goodwill impairments, acquired-intangible amortisation and legal provisions; the model works from underlying EBITDA and charges the cash consequences explicitly (DPA, provisions and deferred consideration in the bridge, a recurring allowance in the flows). Net debt is the company's adjusted net debt at 30 June 2026 (3,599) less lease liabilities (335); it already nets out GBP 198m of cash held for customers and includes GBP 50m of swap liabilities. total_debt is gross debt 3,673 plus swaps 50; cash is the balancing net figure (504 cash less 198 customer cash plus 154 other debt-related items). last_fcf and reported_fcf are the FY2025 GROUP figures (levered, including CEE and separately disclosed cash costs) and are not directly comparable to the unlevered continuing-operations build; year-one unlevered owner FCF in the base case is about GBP 345m. Timing: year one is FY2026, of which H1 is already inside the 30 June 2026 net debt; the overlap is small because H1 net cash flow before debt items was GBP 4m. Buybacks: none in FY2019-FY2025, and SBC is under 0.5% of revenue, so the flat share count is close to fact rather than a convention. Caveats: whether the 20% CEE sale has completed (expected Q4 2026) is not confirmed in the filings held; the proceeds are treated as an asset either way. Adjusted net debt may include a small amount of CEE cash or debt at 100%, which would overlap slightly with the CEE equity value in the bridge. No Analysis JSON exists for this ticker; scenario axes are drawn from the FY2025 annual report and the H1 FY2026 results presentation.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2026 guidance of 5-7% constant-currency online NGR growth with flat retail, decelerating; equity CAGR is unusable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-26% 3yr, -16% 5yr) diverges from revenue CAGR (+7%, +8%) by far more than 30 points. Equity fell from GBP 3.3bn to GBP 1.3bn on goodwill impairments (UK GBP 488m in FY2025), the DPA settlement and legal provisions, not on trading, so it is not a growth signal and was not used.
historical_growth.notes: Group basis including CEE, FY2022-FY2025 and FY2020-FY2025. Owner FCF series = reported FCF less SBC less lease principal paid: FY2020 445.4, FY2022 326.0, FY2025 125.8. The decline reflects interest cost rising from GBP 82m to GBP 273m after debt-funded acquisitions, higher capex, and DPA and other separately disclosed cash costs; SBC is not the driver (under 0.5% of revenue throughout). EPS CAGRs are null because statutory EPS is negative in FY2023-FY2025.

base.growth_rationale: Year one is FY2026: H1 continuing revenue grew 7% reported (5% constant currency) and online NGR guidance of 5-7% cc was reiterated, with retail flat. FY2027 slows as UK tax mitigation (less marketing and bonusing) and the absence of a World Cup weigh on NGR.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 guidance is group EBITDA of GBP 910-960m excluding parent fees; midpoint plus ~GBP 15m of BetMGM parent fees on ~GBP 5.0bn revenue is 19.0%, down from 20.6% in FY2025 on the UK Remote Gaming Duty increase (GBP 56m hit in H1). FY2027 takes the full-year effect plus the betting duty rise, with over 50% mitigated per the company. Recovery to 20.5% reflects mitigation and efficiency programmes, and stops short of the FY2025 level.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax applied to unlevered EBIT. Underlying ETR is ~34% on a post-interest base inflated by UK interest-deductibility limits; a 27% rate on EBIT reflects the UK 25%, Australia 30%, Italy and Brazil mix. Year-one tax of ~GBP 130m less the shield on ~GBP 235m of interest is consistent with ~GBP 70-80m of actual cash tax.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 capex guided at c.GBP 290m including licence costs (5.8% of revenue), easing to just above D&A.

scenario_narratives.base: Entain delivers FY2026 guidance (online NGR +5-7% cc, EBITDA GBP 910-960m before parent fees) and mitigates a little over half of the UK gambling duty increases as it has said it will. The margin troughs in FY2027 at just under 19% when the UK changes are fully annualised, then recovers to 20.5% on efficiency programmes and operating leverage in online, still below FY2025. Growth settles from mid-single digits toward 2.5% as UK, Italy, Brazil and Australia mature. BetMGM and the CEE stake are worth what the bridge carries them at, and legal liabilities settle near provisions.
scenario_narratives.bull: UK tax mitigation exceeds 50% as smaller operators exit and Entain takes share (UK online NGR was +13% cc in H1 FY2026); Brazil and Italy compound, and the online margin moves back toward the mid-20s that the business earned before the tax change, lifting group margin to 22.5%. Recurring restructuring and legal costs fade as the DPA and AUSTRAC matters close. The management target of more than GBP 500m of adjusted cash flow from 2028 is met. BetMGM upside (its USD 500m EBITDA ambition) is NOT in this scenario's flows: the bridge value is the same in all three scenarios, so the bull case understates if the US business re-accelerates.
scenario_narratives.bear: Regulation is the axis. Other jurisdictions follow the UK and the Netherlands in raising gambling duty; UK mitigation falls short and NGR stalls as marketing is cut; affordability and advertising restrictions tighten in Australia and Brazil; UK and Irish retail keeps shrinking under fixed lease costs. Margin falls to 17% and stays there, growth runs at inflation or less, and separately disclosed legal and restructuring costs stay elevated (player claims in Germany and Austria, an AUSTRAC penalty above the AUD 100m provided). With net debt at 3.1x EBITDA, equity value is highly geared to this path: most of the bear-case equity is the BetMGM and CEE stakes, not the core business.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: leverage of 3.1x, dependence on tax and regulatory decisions in a handful of jurisdictions (the UK change alone cut GBP 56m from H1 EBITDA and forced a GBP 488m impairment), and open-ended legal exposures (AUSTRAC, German and Austrian player claims). Base held at 50%: guidance has been reiterated and H1 FY2026 was ahead of expectations. Bull cut to 25%: it needs tax mitigation, market-share gains and the end of recurring one-off costs to arrive together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF on continuing operations, built from components off underlying EBITDA with leases, the TAB NZ revenue share and a recurring one-off allowance charged as cash costs, plus a sum-of-parts bridge for the BetMGM joint venture, the Entain CEE stake and identified legal and acquisition liabilities. SBC is immaterial (under 0.5% of revenue), so the house and street bases are close. The equity is a geared residual: enterprise value of the core business is roughly twice the equity, so small changes in margin or the discount rate move value per share a long way.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gambling duty and regulation: further tax rises or affordability and advertising limits in the UK, Australia, Brazil, Italy or the Netherlands flow straight to margin.
Leverage: net debt of GBP 3.6bn at 3.1x EBITDA with maturities from 2028; each 1 point of EBITDA margin is worth roughly 80p per share.

Bridge items are about 40% of base equity value and rest on judgment: BetMGM at 11x post-fee EBITDA (guidance is already at the lower end of its range) and CEE at the price of a 20% sale that had not closed at the last filing.
Legal liabilities may exceed provisions: AUSTRAC (comparable penalties AUD 45m-450m against AUD 100m provided), German and Austrian player claims, and shareholder litigation.
Recurring separately disclosed items: the model allows ~GBP 25m a year in the base case against GBP 65m of non-DPA one-offs guided for FY2026.

TAB NZ: the profit-share payment is modelled as a perpetual cost against a 25-year arrangement whose contingent consideration is carried at GBP 716m; its fixed deferred element is taken from the FY2025 balance sheet.
